heading: ESOP Tax Rules for ITR: Navigating Salary & Capital Gains
tldr: ESOPs are taxed at two distinct stages: when you exercise them and when you sell the shares.
The difference between the Fair Market Value (FMV) on exercise date and the exercise price is taxed as perquisite income.
This perquisite income is added to your salary and reported in your Income Tax Return (ITR) for the financial year of exercise.
When you sell the shares, the difference between the sale price and the FMV on the exercise date is taxed as capital gains.
Proper record-keeping of grant letters, exercise statements, and sale contract notes is crucial for accurate ITR filing.
caption:
Got ESOPs from your company? That's awesome! But knowing how they're taxed can be tricky. Basically, you pay tax in two steps: once when you get the shares, and again when you sell them. Understanding these rules helps you avoid surprises later. Learn the simple steps to handle your ESOP taxes correctly in your ITR. Read more in our article.
